findings.title: GitHub identity is validated by mutable login instead of stable ID
findings.body: OAuthLoginView stores only authenticated_user_info['login'] at line 438, and GitHubInstallation compares that string to integration.metadata['sender']['login']. GitHub logins are mutable and can be renamed or later reclaimed by another account, while webhook sender data and the GitHub user API also provide a stable user ID. Using login can cause legitimate installs to fail after renames and may allow a different account that acquired an old login to pass this ownership check. Compare stable IDs instead.

findings.title: Installation ownership is not validated when the Integration row does not exist
findings.body: If Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation.dispatch immediately calls pipeline.next_step(), which leads build_integration to create the integration using only the supplied installation_id. In that path the newly added github_authenticated_user check is never applied because there is no sender metadata. If the GitHub webhook is delayed or fails, or if an attacker knows or guesses an installation_id that has not yet been recorded, a user who completed GitHub OAuth as any GitHub account may be able to attach that GitHub installation to their own Sentry organization. This path should fail closed or verify ownership before creating the integration.

findings.title: Direct access to metadata sender can raise KeyError
findings.body: The mismatch check accesses integration.metadata['sender']['login'] directly. Integrations created without sender metadata, older rows, or inconsistent metadata will not have this key. In that case the installation flow raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of showing the intended failure page. Use defensive access such as .get and fail closed when sender identity is unavailable.

findings.title: User info lookup failures are not handled gracefully
findings.body: get_user_info(payload['access_token']) is called without exception handling. If GitHub's user endpoint returns an error, times out, rate-limits the request, or otherwise fails after the token exchange, the pipeline dispatch will raise and likely produce a 500. Since this PR is meant to present a controlled failure page for invalid installation requests, this call should catch integration/API errors and return error().

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL parameters are not URL-encoded
findings.body: The redirect to GitHub's OAuth authorize endpoint is built by string interpolation without URL-encoding the query parameters. redirect_uri in particular should be form-url-encoded; if absolute_uri ever includes special characters, query components, or non-ASCII characters, the authorize request may be malformed or rejected. Use urlencode to build the query string.

findings.title: Empty installation_id query parameter is treated as present
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch uses request.GET.get('installation_id', pipeline.fetch_state('installation_id')) and then only checks installation_id is None. A request with installation_id= will bind an empty string and continue the pipeline instead of falling back to the stored state or redirecting to the app URL. This can lead to a confusing downstream failure when build_integration is called with an empty installation ID. Treat empty values as missing.

findings.title: Direct GitHub install redirect does not validate installation_id
findings.body: When provider_id is github and setup_action=install but no pipeline exists, the code reads installation_id from the query string and passes it directly to reverse(). If installation_id is missing, this can generate an invalid redirect or raise an exception depending on URL resolver behavior. Validate that installation_id is present before redirecting, or redirect to a safe default installation flow.

findings.title: Security tests do not cover the main identity-validation edge cases
findings.body: test_github_user_mismatch only exercises a login-string mismatch where webhook sender metadata exists. It does not cover missing sender metadata, stable GitHub user ID comparison, renamed/reclaimed logins, or the path where Integration.DoesNotExist skips ownership validation and proceeds to build_integration. Because this PR is a security fix, these edge cases should have explicit tests.
